 Judgment

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 20.07.2010 passed in MVC No.490/2007 by the Fast Track Court-I and MACT, Kolar (for short 'the Tribunal'), MFA No.9989/2010 is filed by the petitioners therein and MFA Crob.No.163/2011 is filed by respondent No.1 therein.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.
3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 30.04.1998 at about 8.30 p.m. deceased Chikka Venkataramana was traveling in his TVS Astra vehicle bearing registration No.KA-07-E-6585 from Enigadele to Chinnamappalli village.
At that time, the vehicle of respondent No.1 a Hero Honda motor cycle bearing Engine No.09044 and Chasis No.03000 came and dashed against the said TVS Astra vehicle.
Because of which, the deceased suffered grievous injuries and later succumbed to the same.

sentences.text: Petitioners are the dependents of the deceased and they filed MVC No.419/2007 against respondent No.1- who was the owner of the vehicle Hero Honda motor cycle and respondent No.2-insurance company which had duly insured the said motor cycle.
Case of the petitioners is that, the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of Hero Honda motor cycle.
5. After service of summons both the respondents have entered appearance and filed their written statements.

6. Respondent No.1 has denied the accident and contended that even otherwise the vehicle being duly insured respondent No.2-insurance company is liable to pay the compensation, if any, to the petitioners.

7. Respondent No.2-insurance company has also denied the averments made in the claim statement of the petitioners and in addition to that has also taken a contention that the rider of the Hero Honda motor cycle did not have a valid licence as on the date of the accident.
However, it is admitted that the offending Hero Honda motor cycle was duly insured by it.
8. Petitioner No.1 has examined herself as PW.1 and the petitioners to prove their case have produced Exs.P1 to P13.

Respondents have examined three witnesses and have produced Exs.R1 to R5.
9.
The Tribunal based on the pleadings and the evidence let in has come to the conclusion that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of Hero Honda motor cycle.
That the said motor cycle was duly insured with respondent No.2-insurance company.
However, the rider of the motor cycle as on the date was one G.V.Manjunath and he had no valid driving licence.

For the said reason, it has held that the petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,56,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization and respondent No.1-owner of the Hero Honda motor cycle is held liable to pay the said compensation.
10.

Not satisfied by the said compensation awarded, petitioners therein have filed MFA No.9989/2010 seeking enhancement of compensation and respondent No.1 challenging the liability on him, has preferred MFA.Crob.163/2011.
11.
The petitioners in their claim statement have categorically contended that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the Hero Honda motor cycle belonging to respondent No.1.
PW.1 has also stated the same in her evidence.
However, evidence of PW.1 in this regard is hearsay as she is not an eye witness to the accident.

However, Tribunal based upon Ex.P1-FIR and complaint, Ex.P2-copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P3-copy of seizure mahazar, Ex.P4-copy of P.M. report and Ex.P5-copy of IMV report, has come to the conclusion that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the Hero Honda motor cycle.

12. Further, in the course of arguments learned counsel for the petitioners as well as respondents submit that pursuant to the FIR and complaint lodged against rider of the motor cycle, chargesheet G Vijayalashmi vs B L Prasad Reddy on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165606563/
4 has been filed against him in CC No.205/2000.

13. Nevertheless, chargesheet is filed after due investigation by the police and in the instant case,
police are of the opinion that the accident has been caused by the rash and negligent driving of the rider of Hero Honda motor cycle.

Further, it is noted that respondent No.1-owner of the offending motor cycle has not contended in his written statement that the accident has not taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the Hero Honda motor cycle nor PW.1 has been cross-examined by respondent No-1 on this count.

Further, it is also seen that RW.1 rider of the Hero Honda motor cycle has not taken a contention in his examination-in-chief that the accident did not occur because of his rash and negligent driving.

Thus, based on the pleadings and evidence let in, Tribunal has rightly come to the conclusion that rider of the Hero Honda motor cycle was responsible for causing the accident by rash and negligent driving.

14. Next question that arises for consideration is 'whether the rider of the Hero Honda motor cycle had a valid driving licence or not and whether the insurance company has discharged its liability of proving that he did not have a valid driving licence?

15. It is the specific case of respondent No.1 that he had a valid driving licence and that onus of proving it otherwise is on the insurance company and that respondent No.2-insurance company has not discharged its burden of proving the same and the Tribunal erred in coming to the conclusion that insurance company had proved the same and has erroneously fixed liability on respondent No.1.
16.
RW.1 was riding the offending vehicle Hero Honda motor cycle on the date of the accident.
He has deposed that at the time of the accident he lost his driving licence.
However, he has also deposed that he has not lodged any police complaint in this regard.
Subsequently, he also deposed that he took driving licence from Kolar RTO and he has contended that he had a valid driving licence as on the date of the accident.
But it is seen that he has not taken any steps to produce copy of the said driving licence or any endorsement to effect from the concerned RTO to that effect.

17. Per contra, respondent No.2-insurance company has taken a specific plea in its written statement that driver - 10 - of the offending vehicle did not have a valid driving licence as on the date of the accident and they examined RW.1 in this regard.

Insurance company has also examined the RTO, Kolar as RW.2 and he has specifically stated that pursuant to the notice of Court he has got search done from the records in his office as to whether RW.1 was issued any driving licence and could not find any driving licence being issued to RW.1 (rider of Hero Honda motor cycle).
18.
It is contended by respondent No.1 that in the cross-examination RW.2 has stated that he did not personally searched the volumes.

He being an officer heading the said office, it is sufficient that if he G Vijayalashmi vs B L Prasad Reddy on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165606563/
5 gets the search done from his sub-ordinates and it is not required for him to search licence himself from the record books.

19. Respondent No.1 has relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Narchinva V. Kamat &

sentences.text:
paragraphs 14 and 15 are held as follows:
"14.
The last question is whether he had a valid driving licence.
The High Court has not recorded a clear cut finding on this point.
The finding of the Tribunal is more evasive than the one by the High Court.
Mr. Sharma did not dispute that the second appellant had a driving licence.

His grievance is that he having failed to produce the same when called upon to do so in the cross-examination, an adverse inference be drawn against him that he did not have a valid licence to drive a pick-up van.
The submission fails to carry conviction with us.
The burden to prove that there was breach of the contract of insurance was squarely placed on the shoulders of the insurance company.
It could not be said to have been discharged by it by a mere question in cross- examination.
The second appellant was under no obligation to furnish evidence so as to enable the insurance company to wriggle out its liability under the contract of insurance.
Further the R.T.A. which issues the driving licence keeps a record of the licences issued and renewed by it.
The insurance company could have got the evidence produced to substantiate his allegation.
Applying the test who would fail if no evidence is led, the obvious answer is the insurance company.

To sum up the insurance company failed to prove that there was a breach of the terms of the contract of insurance as evidenced by the policy of insurance on the ground that the driver who was driving the vehicle at the relevant time did not have a valid driving licence.

Once the insurance company failed to prove that aspect, its liability under the contract of insurance remains intact and unhampered and it was bound to satisfy the award under the comprehensive policy of insurance."
20.

Based on the said judgment, learned counsel for respondent No.1 contends that burden of proving that the rider of the motor cycle did not have driving licence on the date of the accident is on the insurance company and that insurance company has not produced any clinching evidence to prove that he did not have the driving licence.
21. This judgment is of no help to respondent No.1.

No doubt, burden of proving an allegation is on the person who makes it and in the instant case it is the insurance company which has contended G Vijayalashmi vs B L Prasad Reddy on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165606563/
6

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that rider of the motor cycle did not have a valid driving licence at the time of the accident and the burden of proving the same is on the - 13 - insurance company.
It has taken its specific plea to that effect.

It has cross-examined RW.1 who was the rider of the motor cycle wherein it has been suggested to him that he did not have a valid driving licence, for which he has denied the said suggestion but has not produced the same before Court.

Further, insurance company has taken pains to have the same searched with RTO, Kolar and RTO,
Kolar has deposed before the Court that the search did not yield any result showing that a valid licence was issued in favour of rider of motor cycle.

By these acts, in my opinion, under the given circumstances of the case, respondent No.2-insurance company has discharged its burden of proving that driver of the motor cycle did not have a valid driving licence.
It cannot do anything more than that.

Once plea to that effect was taken by insurance company, RW.1 (rider of the motor cycle) was cross-examined and the jurisdictional RTO was examined by it, the onus shifted on RW.1 to prove otherwise and he could have produced a copy of the driving licence at least or particulars of the same which he had not done so.
Thus, in my opinion, Tribunal has concluded rightly that rider - 14 - of the Hero Honda motor cycle did not have a valid driving licence at the time of the accident.

22. Next question that arises for consideration is 'who is liable to compensate the petitioners and what is the quantum of compensation?
23.
A rider driving a motor cycle without a valid driving licence is a serious infraction and insurance company is always entitled to raise that as a ground of defence.
However, it has to be kept in mind the law relating to insurance is a social welfare legislation and in the instant case the offending vehicle was duly insured.

This Court as well as Hon'ble Apex Court in catena of judgment have come to the conclusion that in such circumstances to meet the ends of justice claimants cannot be made to run from pillar to post to execute the awards against owners or riders of vehicles and it would be just and fair to direct the insurance company to pay the compensation with liberty being reserved to them to recover the same from owner of the offending vehicle.

Hence, under the present circumstances, it would be appropriate to direct respondent No.2-insurance company to compensate the petitioners giving it the liberty to recover the same from respondent No.1-owner of the offending motor cycle.
25. In respect of quantum of compensation, based on the evidence let in by the parties, Tribunal has come to the conclusion that income of the deceased was Rs.6,000/- p.m.
No cogent reasons are adduced by any of the parties as to why the same requires to be altered.
Hence, income of the deceased is considered at Rs.6,000/- p.m.
Deceased was aged 36 years at the time of the accident.

sentences.text: Further, the deceased, who had two dependants - 16 - at the time of his death, 1/3rd of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Thus, on the count of 'loss of dependency', the petitioners would be entitled to a sum of Rs.10,08,000/- (Rs.6,000/- x 12 x 15 + 40% x 2/3).
Petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of estate and funeral expenses'.
Each of the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of consortium', together they are entitled to a sum of Rs.80,000/- under the said head.
Thus, the petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.11,18,000/- as against Rs.7,56,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Further, given the bank rate of interest, in my opinion, it is appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the compensation amount from the date of petition before Tribunal till realization.

Further, the deceased, who had two dependants - 16 - at the time of his death, 1/3rd of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Thus, on the count of 'loss of dependency', the petitioners would be entitled to a sum of Rs.10,08,000/- (Rs.6,000/- x 12 x 15 + 40% x 2/3).
Petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of estate and funeral expenses'.
Each of the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of consortium', together they are entitled to a sum of Rs.80,000/- under the said head.
Thus, the petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.11,18,000/- as against Rs.7,56,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Further, given the bank rate of interest, in my opinion, it is appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the compensation amount from the date of petition before Tribunal till realization.
